absent: Layout and defaults of ot_test, ot_data and ot_obj_stat and meaning of bulk, delay, duration, timer, object size, mode, async and name fields.
Value of OT_NR_MAX_BULK and bounds checking for bulk depths against it.
Behavior and contracts of objpool init, fini, pop, push and drop.
Full body of test_parman_check_array beyond ordering check and bodies of test_parman_lsort, test_parman_init and test_parman_exit not shown in part one fragment.
Semantics of parman library types and operations including create, destroy, priority init and fini, item add and remove, and list sort algorithm type.
Concrete numeric identities for module name, allocation flags, clock and timer modes, timer restart codes, and negative error codes.
Synchronization and timing primitives behavior for read write semaphore, completion, hrtimer, kthread, sleep, timeout, preemption control, deferred reclamation, timekeeping and jiffy conversion.
Per CPU, cpu mask and allocation helpers behavior for per CPU access, possible and online CPU handling, zeroed allocation, release, reallocation and deterministic random helpers.
Logging and diagnostic behavior for informational, error and warning helpers.
Error handling for timer setup failure inside per CPU init whose status is ignored by callers.

findings.text: Per CPU test record holds pool reference, test parameters reference, worker callback for thread versus timer context, timer cycle plus timer object, two bulk depths for normal and timer paths, delay value, iteration counter, two statistics buckets for normal and timer activity, and elapsed duration. Initialization clears the record then installs supplied pool, test and worker and copies bulk and delay settings from test parameters and attempts timer setup.

Pool element carries opaque owner pointer, numeric data field, reference counter, and fixed payload area of thirty two unsigned words. Element initializer records address of enclosing pool head as owner and reports success, establishing ownership linkage used later for validation.

Synchronization test context embeds pool head, test parameters reference, user buffer pointer with size, and deferred reclamation callback head. Buffer pointer and size appear unused by shown logic beyond storage, while pool head and test reference drive init, run and teardown and callback head enables deferred teardown in async mode.

Priority wrapper pairs library priority object with numeric priority value. Item wrapper pairs library item object with owning priority wrapper reference and usage flag. Harness state holds library handle, dynamic pointer array with limit, fixed priority table and fixed item table sized by test constants, deterministic random state, run and bulk budgets with bulk idle flag, and used item count.

Compact node size equals size of pool element structure. Large node size equals five hundred twelve. Test table uses compact versus large to exercise different allocation paths and allocation flag selection.

Priority table sizing derives from shift seven giving one hundred twenty eight entries with mask one less. Item table sizing derives from shift thirteen giving eight thousand one hundred ninety two entries with mask one less. Masks support wrapping random indexes into tables.

Base array capacity derives from shift eight giving two hundred fifty six. Resize granularity derives from shift seven giving one hundred twenty eight. Bulk maximum shift equals two plus resize step shift giving nine and count five hundred twelve with mask one less. Total run budget equals item count scaled by two hundred fifty six. Pointer array footprint equals entry count scaled by size of one item wrapper pointer. Sort operations advertise base and step values above with list sort algorithm selection.

Allocation wrapper tracks successful zeroed allocations in allocation counter and ignores failures. Free wrapper ignores null pointers and otherwise tracks size in free counter before releasing. Reporter logs allocation versus free deltas separately for two allocators, so imbalance indicates leak. Counters are long atomics within test data.

Both sync and async initializers size pool at possible CPU count scaled by eight and default to blocking allocation, switching to atomic allocation when object size is below five hundred twelve. Failure to allocate context or to initialize pool releases context and signals failure with null. Successful init expects object count to match requested maximum.

Per CPU initializer clears record and installs pool, test and worker, copies normal and timer bulk depths and delay from test parameters, and delegates timer setup. Timer setup reports missing timer when period is zero and otherwise converts millisecond period to cycle duration and registers monotonic relative timer with shared handler.

Worker thread increments thread count, waits on shared start gate, captures start time, arms optional timer, then loops invoking worker in thread mode until stop flag observed or stop requested, then disarms timer, records microsecond duration, and completes shared wait when last thread exits. Timer start and stop are no ops when timer period disabled.

Timer handler resolves enclosing per CPU record from timer object, checks stop flag with acquire semantics and terminates without rearm when set, otherwise invokes worker in timer mode, advances timer by configured cycle, and requests restart.

Synchronous run initializes pool through mode selected operations, holds write gate while preparing per CPU records and launching one pinned thread per online CPU, briefly sleeps to let threads block, handles zero thread case by completing wait, releases gate to start, sleeps for configured duration, publishes stop with release semantics, waits for thread completion, tears down pool, then emits performance and memory reports.

Asynchronous run mirrors synchronous launch and timed stop but finalizes through deferred reclamation rather than immediate teardown. Finalizer queues callback that asserts stop observed, finalizes pool and completes reclamation signal. Run waits for both thread completion and reclamation completion before reporting. Release callback validates head and context linkage, frees context and reports success.

Bulk operations pop up to bulk depth objects then iterate in reverse, incrementing reference count on success and counting hit, counting miss on null. Thread path may sleep for configured delay periodically. Async variant samples stop flag and disables preemption around reclamation decision in thread mode, pushing back for reuse when running and dropping permanently when stopping. Sync variant always pushes back.

Creation allocates harness, sizes pointer array to base capacity, creates library instance, seeds random state, initializes unique priorities and random item to priority assignments, and sets run budget, unwinding array and harness on failure. Destruction removes used items, finalizes priorities, destroys library, releases array and frees harness.

Randomized run walks items cyclically from random start while budgets allow. Budget checker decrements run budget to terminate and periodically refreshes bulk budget and idle flag from random bits. When idle, iteration is skipped. Otherwise unused item is added through library and recorded in array with used count increment, while used item is cleared from array and removed with count decrement, toggling usage flag. Addition error aborts run.

Resize grows or shrinks pointer array through reallocating allocator, treating zero size as success without further update, failing on allocation failure, zeroing newly added tail on growth, then publishing new array and limit. Move shifts a span within array and clears source span, preserving array limit.

Random state is seeded with fixed constant. Priority generator draws random values, rejects zero, and rejects duplicates against already assigned priorities, retrying until unique nonzero value found. Priority init assigns such value to each table entry and registers it with library.

Visible validation requires array limit at least base capacity, forbids gaps when caller disallows them, counts populated entries, and requires priorities to appear in nondecreasing order along array, reporting violations through error log and error status. Full routine beyond ordering check is not shown in this fragment.

Data initializer clears test data, initializes start gate and two completion signals, and sets thread count to one to account for starter. Performance reporter skips per CPU records with zero duration, aggregates thread and timer hits and misses per CPU and globally, logs per CPU and total durations and counts, and stores totals and duration back into test data for final summary.

Static table holds ten configurations spanning sync versus async, compact versus large object size, with variations for timer use and bulk depth and delay. Durations share common value while bulk, timer and delay fields distinguish normal, timer driven, overrun and async behaviors. Module init selects sync or async starter by per entry flag.

Read write semaphore gates start with starter holding write while preparing threads and workers taking read to block until release. Thread count atomic plus wait completion signals all workers finished, with starter decrement handling zero worker case. Stop flag atomic published with release and observed with acquire coordinates termination. Separate completion coordinates deferred reclamation in async mode.

Async thread path disables preemption around stop sampling and object reclamation to stabilize per CPU context, reenabling afterwards. Timer path omits this protection. Teardown orders stop publication before deferred callback, and callback asserts stop visibility before finalizing pool, ensuring all CPUs observe termination before resources reclaimed.

Module init iterates static test table, initializes per test synchronization data, dispatches each entry to async or sync starter by flag, then logs aggregate duration with hit and miss totals per entry and returns retry signal to prevent retention. Module exit performs no action.

Thread creation failure is only logged and run continues, risking reduced concurrency and reliance on timeout path. Null pop results are treated as miss rather than error, masking exhaustion. Optional timer leaves timer object uninitialized when disabled. Pool init failure aborts run with out of memory status without further reporting.

Resize failure propagates as error and can abort creation or run, leaving prior array intact. Run aborts on first library addition error without rolling back already applied toggles in that iteration beyond counted state. Creation unwinds only array and harness on library failure, relying on earlier steps having no other resources.

Per CPU storage provides one test record per CPU for both sync and async runs. Sync and async operation tables each expose init and fini callbacks with single mode entry, allowing mode indexed dispatch. Sync finalizer finalizes pool then frees context using test reference stored in context.
Logging prefix macro prepends module name to every formatted message in parman test, ensuring uniform identification of diagnostics without changing call sites.
